record.context_brief: Whether the fifth Singer transfer stays an isomorphism for t at least two
record.original_question: For every integer t ≥ 2, is the rank-5 Singer transfer Tr_5 an isomorphism in bidegree (5, 5 + (13·2^t - 5))? Using the reductions explained in the paper, this amounts to determining the GL_5-invariants of (QP_5)_{47}, where QP_5 = P_5/A_2^+P_5 for P_5 = F_2[x_1,…,x_5], and in particular understanding whether the invariant subspace of Ker((Sqg^0_*)(5,47)) vanishes. The paper also highlights a more interesting alternative in which this kernel has nontrivial GL_5-invariants and dim((QP_5)^{GL_5}_{47}) is not equal to 1.

evidence.quote: To end this introduction, we will discuss whether Tr_5 is an isomorphism or not in the bidegree (5, 5 + (13.2^t - 5)) for t ≥ 2.

From these data with the fact that h_{t+1}f_{t-1} ∈ Im(Tr_5) for t ≥ 1, we conclude that if (Ker(Sqg^0_*)(5,13.2^2-5))^{GL_5} is zero, then Tr_5 is an isomorphism in the bidegree (5, 5 + (13.2^t - 5)) for every t ≥ 2.
However, it will be much more interesting if (Ker(Sqg^0_*)(5,13.2^2-5))^{GL_5} is non-trivial and dim(QP_5)^{GL_5}_{13.2^2-5} ≠ 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over the field $\mathbb{F}_2$. Let $\mathcal{A}$ denote the mod-2 Steenrod algebra and let $P_h = \mathbb{F}_2[x_1,\dots,x_h]$ be the polynomial algebra on $h$ generators of degree 1, regarded as a left $\mathcal{A}$-module. Let $\mathcal{A}_2^+ \subset \mathcal{A}$ denote the augmentation ideal, and define the "hit quotient"
$$QP_h \;=\; P_h/\mathcal{A}_2^+ P_h \;=\; \mathbb{F}_2 \otimes_{\mathcal{A}} P_h.$$
The general linear group $GL_h = GL_h(\mathbb{F}_2)$ acts on $P_h$ by linear substitution and this action descends to $QP_h$; write $(QP_h)^{GL_h}_d$ for the subspace of $GL_h$-invariants in internal degree $d$. Singer's algebraic transfer is a homomorphism
$$Tr_h : (\mathbb{F}_2 \otimes_{GL_h} (QP_h)^*)_d \longrightarrow \operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal{A}}_{h, h+d}(\mathbb{F}_2, \mathbb{F}_2),$$
defined for each rank $h \geq 1$ and each internal degree $d \geq 0$. Let $Sq^0_*$ denote the classical squaring (Kameko) operation acting on $QP_h$ in the relevant degrees, and let $\bigl(\operatorname{Ker}(Sq^0_*)\bigr)(h, d)$ be its kernel in bidegree $(h,d)$.

Question. For every integer $t \geq 2$, is the rank-5 Singer transfer
$$Tr_5 : \bigl(\mathbb{F}_2 \otimes_{GL_5} (QP_5)^*\bigr)_{13\cdot 2^t - 5} \longrightarrow \operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal{A}}_{5,\, 5 + (13\cdot 2^t - 5)}(\mathbb{F}_2, \mathbb{F}_2)$$
an isomorphism? Equivalently, determine the $GL_5$-invariants $(QP_5)^{GL_5}_{13\cdot 2^2 - 5} = (QP_5)^{GL_5}_{47}$, and in particular decide whether
$$\bigl(\operatorname{Ker}(Sq^0_*)(5, 47)\bigr)^{GL_5} \;=\; 0,$$
in which case $Tr_5$ is an isomorphism in bidegree $(5,\, 5+(13\cdot 2^t - 5))$ for every $t \geq 2$. Alternatively, exhibit the more interesting situation in which this kernel of $GL_5$-invariants is nontrivial and $\dim (QP_5)^{GL_5}_{47} \neq 1$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turned up many recent works on Singer's conjecture for the algebraic transfer (rank 4 confirmed, rank 5 known to fail in internal degree 108, rank 6 negation results), but none of the located sources explicitly settle whether $Tr_5$ is an isomorphism in bidegree $(5,\,5+(13\cdot 2^t-5))$ for all $t\geq 2$, nor whether $(\operatorname{Ker}(Sq^0_*)(5,47))^{GL_5}=0$. The status of this specific family of bidegrees could not be confirmed from the search.

status_evidence.title: Singer's algebraic transfer for all ranks s ≥ 5 and the negation of Singer's conjecture for rank six
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work establishes failure of Singer's conjecture for the sixth algebraic transfer and discusses rank-5 cases (e.g., internal degree 108).
status_evidence.claim: Rank-5 Singer transfer is known in only some specific internal degrees; the family $13\cdot 2^t-5$ is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: On Singer's conjecture for the fifth algebraic transfer
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the rank-5 transfer and identifies bidegrees where it is or might fail to be an isomorphism.
status_evidence.claim: No definitive resolution found in the located literature for the bidegrees $(5,5+(13\cdot 2^t-5))$, $t\ge 2$.
